scope.summary: BkGui integration test per Section 13.27 GUI clauses: a no-context model drives a complete channel-edit -> capture -> verify loop through Argus alone — discover the pane from the accesskit tree, set a breast-volume channel to an over-range value by author_id, capture the viewport, and verify both control state and rendered change without any GUI-shell manual interaction.
acceptance_criteria: The test starts from zero UI knowledge: enumerate the accesskit tree, locate the BodyKit tab and the breast volume slider purely by author_id conventions documented in the UserManual chapter.

It sets the slider to a designed over-range value, confirms the CRDT edit landed (get_body shows the new channel value), captures the viewport, and verifies the capture differs from the baseline (image hash delta).
The whole flow runs headless in CI with no foreground window, no focus steal, and a clean console error scan (quiet-mode compliance).
Failure output includes the accesskit tree snapshot and the last capture so a no-context model can diagnose without re-running.
The flow is documented as the reference Argus recipe in the UserManual BodyKit chapter (MT-651 cross-link).

The exact TailorSurfaceDescriptor row MT-635 enumerates every route, pane, control author_id, dynamic entity-key rule, action, state, help anchor, permission, undo policy, receipt, and command binding; wildcard-only evidence is rejected.

Applicable blank, loading, populated, stale/conflict, cancelled, failed, retry, permission, keyboard/focus, narrow/4K/DPI, overlap/clipping, and no-focus-steal states are covered by the registry-derived Argus matrix.
scope.risk_if_missed: The GUI claims model-operability without proof; the first real agent session discovers unreachable controls or unstable ids mid-production, and the HBR-VIS/INT posture for BodyKit is built on an untested assumption.

target_entries: Tailor UserManual > BodyKit workspace and controls

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: This MT owns authoritative, job, or external-tool lifecycle events and must project the same event_id, run_id, actor_id, and correlation_id from EventLedger into Flight Recorder.
This MT must wire the shared internal_diagnostics API for its native, job, device, solver-run, or DCC failure modes with bounded structured evidence.
Long-running, native, or external-process work must register bounded progress and child/process identity with the shared Palmistry watcher; Tailor must not fork a watcher.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.

required_changes_before_execution: BodyKit GUI must expose or integrate the geometry/morph, joint, weight/rigidity, transfer, skin/material, interlink, Jobs, Problems, history, recovery, and shared-world contracts.
Consume the signed technical refinement, canonical command/surface registries, classified HBR tiers, and task-oriented UserManual contract before execution.
